recentItems.title: The Uprising: How 1381 Was Recreated for Andrew Garfield’s Movie | HISTORY This Week
recentItems.description:
1381. In the English countryside, one peasant has had enough. His resistance leads tens of thousands of armed peasants to march on London. They’re furious about taxes, about wages held down by law, about a world that feels abandoned by God. But they aren’t marching to overthrow the king. They are marching to rescue him.
Paul Greengrass and Dan Jones join Sally Helm to talk about The Uprising, the new film starring Andrew Garfield as a fictional plowman who becomes the face of England's Peasants' Revolt. They get into what life was actually like a generation after the Black Death, why the rebels burned every written record they could find, and how a disturbed 14-year-old king ended up as the last hope of the people marching on his city.

Paul Greengrass is the writer and director of The Uprising, in theaters now. Dan Jones is the film's historical advisor and the author of Summer of Blood. You can follow him at danjones.substack.com for more.

recentItems.title: What Really Killed Bruce Lee? | History's Greatest Mysteries (S2, E3)
recentItems.description:
Bruce Lee died suddenly in 1973 at just 32 years old, weeks before Enter the Dragon would make him a global superstar. His death was officially attributed to a fatal reaction to a painkiller—but decades of rumors have raised questions about poisoning, organized crime, secret health problems and possible foul play.

At the request of Bruce's brother Robert, former Hong Kong police detective Philip Chan reexamines previously unreleased records, witness accounts and Bruce Lee's autopsy to determine what really happened. History's Greatest Mysteries (S2, E3) follows the evidence toward a new explanation for the sudden death of one of the world's most iconic martial artists.
